summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, chronic systolic heart failure (EF 20%), BOOP, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease, was admitted with abdominal pain and bilious vomiting. He reported left flank pain radiating to the groin, consistent with a passed kidney stone, and drainage from a recurrent perirectal abscess. CT imaging confirmed mild left hydroureteronephrosis and soft tissue thickening with central hypodensity at the prior abscess site. He underwent incision and drainage with drain placement and was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later narrowed to oral Augmentin. His acute heart failure exacerbation improved with IV Lasix, and his kidney function remained stable. He was discharged to an extended care facility on home medications, including antibiotics, with follow-up planned in colorectal and orthopedic clinics.
